items.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: John Lewis had to get us out... John Lewis, we ran into him in a bad way.

ctx.x: Yeah, what was the reason to move back to New York.

I just followed... well... Ornette’s old band went back, and we couldn’t live without them at that point. We followed them to Lenox School of Music. I don’t want everything to sound like I was poor. I wasn’t poor. But I didn’t have any money, so, me and Paul

Bley slept underneath the piano at Lenox, on the stage at Lenox. And John Lewis had to get us out, and he wouldn’t let us into the cafeteria cause we weren’t students. So we left after about 3 days and went to New York City, and finally there Ornette and Don and Charlie and Billy, came to New York and starting playing at the Five Spot, and we just hung out there all the time. And we didn’t have to pay to get in, somehow we managed to get into clubs free. Paul Bley always managed to get into clubs for free.
